customers.name: Corporate Legal Counsel / Company Secretary
customers.description: In-house legal counsel or company secretary in the group legal function of a multinational with twenty to three hundred legal entities spread over thirty to sixty jurisdictions, the same groups whose tax teams run their transfer pricing documentation on Reptune.net (companies of the size of TomTom, Stahl, Avnet or Ravago). Keeps the corporate register of every entity current: incorporations, mergers and liquidations, shareholders and share capital, directors and supervisory boards, authorised signatories and powers of attorney, articles, registry extracts and board minutes. Drafts, negotiates and signs the intercompany service, licence, distribution, loan and cost-sharing agreements that give the group's transfer pricing policy its legal form, and is the person the tax team, auditors, banks and acquirers call when they need a structure chart as at a given date. Reports to the General Counsel and works with the Head of Tax, group finance, local directors and outside counsel; is judged on whether the corporate record is accurate and defensible on the day someone asks, and on whether every intercompany transaction has a signed agreement behind it.
careAbout: One time-stamped record per legal entity, shareholder, director and authorised signatory, so any question about who owned or could sign for an entity on a given date is answered from the system rather than from a scanned extract

Every intercompany transaction in the transfer pricing register matched to a signed, in-force agreement with the right parties, term, pricing clause and governing law, before the Local File that describes it is generated
Signature rounds for dozens of agreements that finish in days across time zones, with signatory authority verified against the register and a complete audit trail of who signed what and when

Corporate documents, articles, registry extracts, powers of attorney and board resolutions filed against the entity they belong to and retrievable in seconds during an audit, a financing or a due diligence
Current and historical legal structure charts that come out of the entity data itself and match the Master File, the CbCR and the statutory accounts without redrawing them in a drawing tool

A shared system of record with the tax team, so entity names, addresses, functions and agreements appear identically in the documentation and in the legal files and neither team maintains a copy of the other's data
winsThem: A legal module that stores entity data with an effective date and full history, so the same record can be read as of today or as of the balance-sheet date of any prior year
An intercompany agreement repository reconciled against the transfer pricing transaction register, with gaps, expiries and unsigned drafts surfaced as actions rather than discovered in an audit
DocuSign integration that generates the agreement, sends it to the signatories recorded on the entity, tracks the envelope and files the signed copy back against the transaction
Structure charts generated from shareholdings and entity data for any date, exported for boards, banks, auditors and the Master File, and updated the moment a corporate event is recorded
Access rights per entity, region and role, ISO 27001-certified security and single sign-on, so local directors, outside counsel and auditors see exactly what they are entitled to and nothing else
theirFear: A tax authority or acquirer asking for the signed agreement behind an intercompany transaction and legal finding only an unsigned draft or a version whose parties no longer exist
A structure chart in the Master File that contradicts the shareholder register or the statutory accounts because it was redrawn by hand months after the last restructuring
An agreement signed by a director whose appointment had already ended, discovered only when the counterparty or a court challenges its validity

jobsToBeDone.name: Keep every legal entity and signatory record accurate and time-stamped
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Maintain a single, dated corporate record for every legal entity in the group: identity, registration numbers, addresses, share capital and shareholders, directors, supervisory boards, authorised signatories and powers of attorney, fiscal year and statutory auditor, with the history of every change. The record has to serve the legal function, the tax team that scopes Local Files per entity, finance, auditors, banks and any buyer or seller in a transaction, and it has to be provably correct as at any historical date.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every entity, shareholding, director and signatory is recorded once with effective dates and the supporting corporate documents, changes are captured within days of the corporate event, the tax and finance teams read entity data from the same record instead of maintaining their own lists, and the legal counsel can answer who owned or could sign for an entity on any date without searching e-mail or registry archives.

steps.step: Build the entity master from registers and corporate documents
steps.description: Load every legal entity of the group with its registration numbers, seat, addresses, legal form, share capital, fiscal year and statutory auditor from registry extracts, articles and the group's existing entity lists, using bulk upload from Excel where the group already holds the data. Reconcile the legal list with the entities the tax team has in the transfer pricing model and with the consolidation scope so one entity universe serves legal, tax and finance.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the legal entity records with registration data, addresses, legal form and share capital, bulk-loaded from Excel and registry extracts, as the single source of truth for the group's entities.

streamsNeeded.name: Set Up the Transfer Pricing Model
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shares the same entity universe with the transfer pricing model so the entities legal maintains are the entities the tax team scopes, documents and reports on.

steps.step: Record shareholders, directors and authorised signatories with effective dates
steps.description: Enter for each entity the shareholders and their percentage, the directors and board members with appointment and resignation dates, the authorised signatories with their signing authority and limits, and the powers of attorney in force, so that the register shows both who holds each role today and who held it at any previous date.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Stores shareholders, directors, signatories and powers of attorney as time-stamped records with start and end dates, so the register can be read as of any date.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate with ERP, Operational TP and Identity
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies custom user profiles and access rights so only the legal function can change register data while local directors and the tax team have read access to their entities.

steps.step: Process corporate events as dated changes rather than overwrites
steps.description: When an entity is incorporated, merged, renamed, re-domiciled or liquidated, or a director or signatory changes, record the event with its effective date and the resolution or registry filing behind it, so the previous state is preserved and the tax team is told which entities enter or leave the documentation scope for the fiscal year.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Records incorporations, mergers, name changes, liquidations and role changes as dated events with full history and the linked corporate document.

streamsNeeded.name: Scope and Plan the Annual Documentation Cycle
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Picks up entities that were added, merged or liquidated during the fiscal year so the documentation scope and the deadlines per entity reflect the legal reality.

steps.step: File corporate documents against the entity they belong to
steps.description: Store articles of association, registry extracts, shareholder registers, board and shareholder resolutions, powers of attorney, certificates of good standing and tax residence certificates in the corporate document repository, linked to the entity, the role or the event they evidence, with the version and the date they were obtained.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Holds the corporate document repository with documents linked to entities, roles and corporate events, versioned and retrievable by entity and document type.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Compliance and Defend Audits
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Makes the corporate documents available as audit evidence next to the Local Files so a tax residence certificate or a board resolution is found in the same place as the documentation it supports.

steps.step: Share entity data with tax, finance and auditors under controlled access
steps.description: Give the transfer pricing team, group finance, local directors, outside counsel and auditors access to the entity records they need, with single sign-on, read-only and location-restricted profiles, and let the Master File and Local Files pull entity names, addresses, ownership and management data directly from the register instead of from a copied table.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate with ERP, Operational TP and Identity
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides single sign-on, custom user profiles and read-only or location-restricted access so each stakeholder sees the entities and documents they are entitled to.

streamsNeeded.name: Generate Master File and Local Files
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Inserts entity identity, ownership and management data from the legal record into the organisational sections of the Master File and each Local File without re-keying.

jobsToBeDone.name: Cover every intercompany transaction with a signed agreement
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Make sure that every intercompany transaction the tax team documents, from management and shared services to licences, distribution, contract manufacturing, loans and cash pooling, rests on a written agreement that is signed by authorised representatives of both parties, in force for the period, consistent with the transfer pricing policy and the functional analysis, and available in the language and form the local tax authority expects. Includes drafting from templates, routing for e-signature, tracking renewals and amendments, and keeping the signed copy where the documentation can use it.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every transaction in the intercompany transaction register is linked to a signed, in-force agreement whose parties, term, pricing clause and governing law match the Local File, unsigned drafts and expired agreements are surfaced as actions well before generation, signature rounds close in days through DocuSign, and the signed agreements are inserted into the documentation automatically.

steps.step: Reconcile the transaction register against the agreement repository
steps.description: Compare the intercompany transactions the tax team has registered per entity and fiscal year with the agreements on file, and list transactions without an agreement, agreements whose parties, term or subject no longer match the transaction, and agreements that exist only as unsigned drafts, so the gaps are known months before the Local Files are generated.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Links each agreement to the transactions and entities it covers and reports transactions without an in-force agreement and agreements without a matching transaction.

streamsNeeded.name: Set Up the Transfer Pricing Model
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the intercompany transaction register with transaction types, parties and methods that the agreements must mirror.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Compliance and Defend Audits
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows uncovered transactions as a risk indicator per entity and country on the compliance dashboard so tax and legal prioritise the same gaps.

steps.step: Draft agreements from templates aligned with the transfer pricing policy
steps.description: Generate service, licence, distribution, manufacturing, loan and cost-contribution agreements from group templates whose remuneration clauses reflect the transfer pricing method and the arm's-length range documented for that transaction type, fill in parties, effective dates and governing law from the entity records, and route the draft to tax for a policy check before it goes to signature.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates agreement drafts from group templates with parties, addresses and signatories filled from the entity records and stores each version in the repository.

streamsNeeded.name: Benchmark Intercompany Transactions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the transfer pricing method and arm's-length range per transaction type so the remuneration clause in the agreement matches what the Local File will defend.

steps.step: Route agreements to authorised signatories through DocuSign
steps.description: Send each agreement to the signatories recorded for both entities, in the order the group's signing rules require, through the DocuSign integration; follow envelope status per agreement, chase signatories who have not signed, and let the platform file the completed envelope with its certificate against the agreement and the transaction.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates, sends, stores and tracks e-signature envelopes for agreements with the signatories taken from the entity's authorised-signatory record.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate with ERP, Operational TP and Identity
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the DocuSign integration and identity checks so envelopes are created from the platform and completed documents return to it automatically.

steps.step: Track terms, renewals, amendments and expiries
steps.description: Keep the term, notice period, renewal mechanism and amendment history of every agreement, get reminded before an agreement expires or a pricing clause must be updated after a new benchmark, and record amendments, terminations and novations after a restructuring so the agreement in force for each fiscal year is unambiguous.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Stores term, renewal and amendment data per agreement and links amendments, terminations and novations to the original agreement and the corporate event.

streamsNeeded.name: Scope and Plan the Annual Documentation Cycle
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Assigns renewal and update tasks with e-mail reminders in the same workflow the tax team uses for the documentation cycle so legal and tax deadlines are planned together.

steps.step: Make the signed agreements part of the Local Files
steps.description: Confirm which agreement version applies to each transaction and fiscal year so the generator can insert or reference the signed agreement in the relevant Local File, and arrange a translation or a local-language counterpart where the country requires agreements in the local language or a specific form.

streamsNeeded.name: Generate Master File and Local Files
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Inserts the archived, signed intercompany agreements automatically into the Local Files of the entities that are party to them.

streamsNeeded.name: Localise and Translate Documentation
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides machine translation with transfer pricing glossaries and human-certified translation for agreements that must be filed in the local language.

jobsToBeDone.name: Produce current and historical structure charts on demand
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Deliver a correct legal structure chart of the group, or of any sub-group, region or division, as it stands today or as it stood on any past date, whenever the board, the tax team, an auditor, a bank, a regulator or a potential acquirer asks for one. The chart must reflect the shareholdings and entities in the register, agree with the Master File, the CbCR and the consolidation, and be produced in minutes rather than redrawn by hand.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Structure charts are generated from the time-stamped entity and shareholding data for any date and any scope, exported in the formats boards, banks and the documentation need, inserted into the Master File and Local Files automatically, and the legal counsel never again maintains a slide deck that drifts from the register.

steps.step: Generate the current chart from the entity and shareholding data
steps.description: Produce the group chart, or a chart per region, division or intermediate holding, from the shareholder percentages, entity types and jurisdictions recorded in the register, with branches, partnerships and dormant entities shown according to the group's conventions, and export it for the board pack, the bank or the auditor.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Draws the current legal structure chart from the entity and shareholding records for any scope and exports it without manual drawing.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate with ERP, Operational TP and Identity
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Controls who can view and export charts for which part of the group through user profiles and location-restricted access.

steps.step: Reproduce the chart as at a historical date
steps.description: Answer an audit, a tax authority, a due-diligence team or the CbCR preparer with the structure as it was at the balance-sheet date of a previous fiscal year or on the date of a specific transaction, generated from the dated history of shareholdings and entities rather than from an old presentation found in an archive.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates historical structure charts from the time-stamped register for any past date and keeps them with the corporate documents of that period.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Compliance and Defend Audits
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Lets the tax team attach the dated chart to the audit evidence for the fiscal year under review.

steps.description: Provide the organisational structure required by the OECD Master File template and the local ownership section of each Local File from the same chart data, and confirm that the constituent entities and their jurisdictions in the CbCR match the entities and shareholdings in the register for the reporting fiscal year.

streamsNeeded.name: Prepare and File CbCR and Notifications

customerJourneyStories.name: From the tax team's licence to a shared legal system of record
customerJourneyStories.summary: A corporate legal counsel at a European industrial group with about 120 entities in 45 countries, whose tax team has run Reptune.net for years, adopts the Legal Module after an audit exposes the gap between the legal files and the transfer pricing documentation, and ends up owning the entity and agreement record that both functions work from.

stages.narrative: A tax audit in Italy asks for the signed intercompany service agreement behind a management fee and for the group structure as at the end of the audited year. The Local File describes the transaction, but legal finds only an unsigned 2019 draft in a shared drive and a structure chart in a slide deck that predates two mergers. The Head of Tax and the General Counsel agree that entity and agreement data must live in one system that both functions maintain.

The Head of Tax mentions that the platform the group already uses for its documentation has a Legal Module with time-stamped entity data, an agreement repository, structure charts and DocuSign, and asks Reptune to show it to legal. In the demo the legal counsel sees the entities the tax team already maintains, agreements linked to transactions, and a chart generated from shareholdings for any date, and notes that the tax team's entity list is already the one legal would have had to build.

The legal counsel compares the Legal Module with the specialised entity management suite the group's outside counsel proposes and with extending the existing document management system. The deciding factors are that the entity and agreement data feed the Local Files directly, that time-stamped history and DocuSign are included, that access can be restricted per entity and region, and that the platform is ISO 27001 certified and already passed the group's vendor review when tax licensed it. The module is priced as an add-on to the group's Enterprise plan, which finance accepts.

The first real use is the European region: forty entities are enriched with shareholders, directors, signatories and registry extracts, the agreements for the audited Italian transactions are located, signed through DocuSign and linked to the transaction register, and the structure chart as at the audited year end is generated from the dated data and handed to the auditors. The audit request is answered in a week instead of a month of searching.

Within two quarters all entities are in the module and legal records every corporate event with its effective date and resolution. The reconciliation of transactions against agreements runs before each documentation cycle, uncovered transactions become tasks with reminders, and the Master File and Local Files pull ownership data and signed agreements from the legal record. The quarterly review with the Head of Tax runs on the same dashboard.

At renewal the legal counsel reports that agreement coverage rose from three quarters of transactions to nearly all, that structure charts are produced the same day, and that the next audit request was answered from the system. The group adds read-only access for its auditors and outside counsel and the legal counsel becomes the reference for other legal departments Reptune introduces the module to.

customerJourneyStories.name: Bringing e-signature and the agreement lifecycle into the group's routine
customerJourneyStories.summary: Having run the entity register in the Legal Module for a year, the company secretary of a multinational with entities in 30 countries adopts the DocuSign integration and the agreement renewal workflow to end the year-end scramble for wet-ink signatures, and later uses the same data for restructuring scenarios and future-dated structure charts.

stages.narrative: The annual update of intercompany agreements after a benchmark refresh means sixty agreements have to be signed by directors in fourteen time zones before year end. Couriered originals, scanned signatures and one agreement signed by a director who had already resigned turn the exercise into a six-week project, and the company secretary decides that signature and renewal must run as a workflow, not as an e-mail campaign.

In the annual account review Reptune's customer success manager shows the DocuSign integration that the group has licensed but not switched on, the renewal reminders in the workflow, and how other clients run a signature round in days with signatories taken from the register. A short call with a legal team already using it convinces the company secretary that the setup is a configuration, not a project.

The company secretary checks with outside counsel in which jurisdictions electronic signatures are valid for intercompany agreements and where a qualified signature or a local-language counterpart is required, verifies that the platform checks signatory authority against the register at the moment of sending, reviews the envelope audit trail and certificate, and confirms with IT that the DocuSign account is covered by the group's existing contract and single sign-on.

The first bounded use is the renewal of all management service agreements for one division: drafts are generated from the template with parties and signatories filled from the register, sent through DocuSign in the order the signing rules require, and filed back against the transactions with their certificates. The round closes in eight days and the tax team sees the signed agreements appear in the Local Files at the next generation.

All agreement types move to the workflow. Expiries and pricing-clause updates are tracked as tasks with reminders, amendments and novations after a small restructuring are recorded against the original agreements, and the company secretary models the planned merger of two holdings as a future-dated scenario whose chart tax uses to assess the documentation impact before the transaction closes.

A year later the year-end signature round is a non-event, signatory authority exceptions have disappeared, and the audit committee receives a report on agreement coverage per entity from the dashboard. The group extends the module to a newly acquired sub-group on day one of integration and asks Reptune for local-language agreement templates for its Latin American entities.

customers.name: Transfer Pricing Adviser at a Tax Advisory Firm
customers.description: Partner or senior manager in the transfer pricing practice of an international network firm's member office or of an independent tax boutique in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany or the United Kingdom, serving ten to forty client groups with five to eighty entities each, mostly mid-sized multinationals without a dedicated in-house transfer pricing team. Prepares Master Files, Local Files, benchmarks and CbCR for those clients every year, licenses Reptune.net to do so at a fraction of the traditional effort instead of building each file in Word, and relies on Reptune's country regulations, translation and specialist support for the countries the firm has no desk in. Leads two to six advisers and is judged on chargeable leverage per adviser, realisation of fixed fees, quality of files under audit, retention of clients from year to year and growth of a recurring compliance practice next to advisory work.
careAbout: Documentation prepared with a fraction of the adviser hours it takes in Word, so a fixed fee per Local File still leaves a margin and junior time goes into analysis rather than formatting

customerJourneyStories.name: From Word templates to a licensed platform practice
customerJourneyStories.summary: A transfer pricing partner at a Dutch independent tax firm with twenty documentation clients lives through the practice's move from Word templates and spreadsheets to a licensed Reptune.net practice, from the lost tender that started it to the renewal in which the firm doubles its client count with the same team.

stages.narrative: The firm loses a tender for a client with thirty entities because its fee per Local File is twice the winning bid, and the year-end review shows a realisation rate on documentation engagements below 60 percent: advisers spend most of their hours collecting data by e-mail and formatting Word files. The partner concludes that the practice cannot grow, or even stay profitable, on the current way of working.

At a transfer pricing conference the partner hears a Head of Tax describe how his group generates all its Local Files from one model on Reptune.net, and shortly after receives a call from Reptune's partner programme, which since the Vortex investment actively approaches advisory firms. A demo on the firm's own anonymised client shows a Master File and eight Local Files generated in an afternoon.

The partner evaluates the platform against two international documentation tools and against building templates in the firm's document system. The decisive points are the price per Local File against the firm's fee, the country regulations and localised templates for clients' countries, strict client separation with client organisations and access profiles, the ISO 27001 certification the firm's risk partner requires, and an explicit understanding of how Reptune's own full-service offering and the firm's clients coexist under the partner terms.

In the free two-week trial the team sets up one client group with twelve entities, loads financials through the Excel templates and generates the full set of Local Files in the firm's house style. Two advisers prepare in three days what took three weeks the year before, and the client's finance director notices that the files are more consistent than the previous year's.

Over the following season all twenty clients are set up as organisations on the firm's licence, data collection runs through templates with reminders, and the partner steers the busy season from the workload view. Review time is spent on functional analysis and benchmark exceptions, and the firm starts proposing fixed-fee annual documentation packages priced on the known cost per file.

At renewal the partner reports adviser hours per Local File cut by more than half and a documentation margin the practice has never had, wins back the lost client at a competitive fee, and moves to a larger licence to serve forty client groups with the same team. The firm becomes a reference partner and refers two of its own clients to Reptune for a direct Enterprise licence with the firm as adviser.

customerJourneyStories.name: Adding countries and languages the firm does not cover
customerJourneyStories.summary: A transfer pricing senior manager at a Belgian member firm of an international network, already running documentation for its clients on Reptune.net, adopts the country regulations, machine translation, R-AI country expert and Reptune specialist support when a key client expands into Latin America and Asia, and ends up offering worldwide coverage as a standard service.

stages.narrative: A long-standing client acquires subsidiaries in Mexico, Brazil, India and Vietnam and asks the firm to keep preparing all its documentation. The network's local offices quote fees per Local File higher than the firm charges for the whole group, respond slowly and use their own formats, and the senior manager fears either losing the client to a Big Four firm or delivering non-compliant files in countries the team has never worked in.

In a Reptune partner webinar on local requirements the senior manager sees how the country regulations, localised templates and local forms cover the new countries, how machine translation with transfer pricing glossaries handles Spanish and Portuguese, and how the R-AI country expert answers local questions in any language. A Reptune specialist explains how Collaborative delivery can add a local review at a fixed rate per file.

The senior manager checks the country content for the four new jurisdictions against the network's own alerts, tests the translation on a previous year's file with a Portuguese-speaking colleague, confirms with the risk partner that certified translation and a specialist review satisfy the firm's quality standards for countries without a local desk, and compares the add-on cost with the local offices' quotes.

The first real use is the Mexican and Brazilian Local Files for the client's fiscal year: thresholds are checked in the country regulations, the files are generated on the localised templates, translated in the platform with a certified review, and a Reptune specialist reviews both from the local perspective. Both files are accepted by the client's local advisers without material changes, at a third of the local offices' quoted fee.

The firm activates machine translation and the R-AI country expert across all its clients, scopes new engagements with the country regulations before pricing, prepares CbCR notifications for every jurisdiction from the platform, and books Reptune specialists as a standing back-up for local reviews. Worldwide coverage becomes a line in every proposal instead of a caveat.

Within two years the firm serves client entities in more than thirty countries without a single subcontracted local file, has won three clients whose previous adviser could not cover their footprint, and has cut subcontracting cost to a small share of its documentation fees. The senior manager sits on Reptune's partner advisory group and asks for local-language agreement templates as the next addition.
